# CXNM - Standard - AND - U - Compliance Corporate Device Health

Marks a fully managed or corporate-owned Android device as non-compliant when it is rooted, Play Integrity does not pass with hardware backing, the Intune app has been tampered with, it runs below Android 16 or the latest security patch is older than the minimum.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Android |
| Scope | User (U) — assign to user groups |
| Type | Compliance |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | UniFy Android Enterprise Baseline v1.5.1 — AND - CP - DEV - Fully-Managed and Corp-Work-Profile - v1.5 (health part), compared with IntuneAdmin Baseline - Android Enterprise - Device Health; OS minimum raised from 13.0 to n-1 (16.0) and patch level added |
| File | [`Baseline_AND_U_Compliance_Corporate_Device_Health.json`](Baseline_AND_U_Compliance_Corporate_Device_Health.json) |

> The OS minimum of 16.0 is n-1 (Android 17 was released on 16 June 2026): a device on the previous major version remains compliant, Android 15 does not. That is stricter than UniFy (13.0) and than the work profile variant (12.0), and deliberately so: the organisation chooses this hardware itself. Before assigning, check in the Intune report how many corporate devices are below 16; if there are many, temporarily set the value to 15.0 rather than not assigning the policy. Patch date 2026-03-01, the same as the rest of the Android set. Both go stale: `node scripts/check-osversion.js`. Block action after a 24-hour grace period, the same as the other compliance policies in the baseline (UniFy additionally sends a push notification immediately). Password and encryption are in Compliance Corporate Password, Defender in Compliance Corporate Defender for Endpoint.

## Properties — 28
